cards.text: Isaiah the prophet has a new message, and this time the guest list is EVERYBODY. He calls the nations, the peoples, the whole earth and all that fills it to come near and listen. Friend, that's the biggest group chat there is, and nobody's on mute.

cards.question: Isaiah has called the whole world in to listen. True or false: he says the LORD is angry with only a few of the nations.

cards.text: The LORD is furious with all their armies too, and Isaiah says He will devote them to destruction and give them over to slaughter. Friend, this is a heavy one, so stay close.

cards.question: Isaiah says the LORD will give the armies of the nations over to slaughter. What does he say will happen to their slain?

answers.text: They will be buried in the valley

cards.text: The stench of their corpses will rise, and the mountains will flow with their blood. Then Isaiah stops looking down and looks UP.

cards.question: Isaiah's message reaches past the earth. True or false: he says the skies will be rolled up like a scroll.
Isaiah says the skies will be rolled up. What does he say their stars will do?

cards.text: Rolled up like a scroll! I've rolled up a LOT of dough in my day, friend, and I never once rolled up the SKY.
Then the LORD Himself speaks. When His sword has drunk its fill in the heavens, it will come down on one people He has devoted to destruction.

cards.question: The LORD says His sword will come down from the heavens on one people by name. Which one?

cards.text: Edom is the nation that came from Esau (Genesis 36:9). Isaiah says the sword of the LORD is bathed in blood and drips with fat, with the blood of lambs and goats and the fat of the kidneys of rams.

cards.question: Lambs, goats and rams. Isaiah says the LORD has a ___ in Bozrah, a great slaughter in the land of Edom.

cards.text: And it's not just lambs and goats. The wild oxen will fall with them, the young bulls with the strong ones.

cards.question: Even the wild oxen will fall in Edom. What does Isaiah say will happen to Edom's land?

answers.text: It will be drenched with blood
It will be washed by a flood
It will be sown with salt

cards.question: Isaiah says the LORD has a day of vengeance and a year of recompense for the cause of ___.

cards.text: Now Isaiah tells what will become of Edom's land. Her streams will turn to tar, her soil to sulfur, and her land will become a blazing pitch.

cards.question: Edom's land will become a blazing pitch. True or false: Isaiah says that fire will burn out by morning.
Isaiah says the smoke over Edom will rise forever, and from generation to generation the land will lie ___.

cards.text: No one will ever again pass through it. Friend, I spent years in the back of a junk drawer, and even THAT place got visitors when somebody needed tape.

cards.question: No people will pass through Edom anymore. Who does Isaiah say will possess it instead?

cards.text: Then Isaiah says the LORD will stretch out a measuring line over Edom. But it's a measuring line of chaos and a plumb line of destruction.

cards.question: With chaos stretched over Edom, Isaiah says no ___ will be left to proclaim a king.

cards.text: All her princes will come to nothing, so there's nobody left to look after Edom's towers and fortresses.

cards.question: Nobody's left to look after Edom's towers and fortresses. What does Isaiah say will grow over them?

cards.text: Then jackals and ostriches move in, with desert creatures, hyenas and wild goats calling to one another. Friend, that's not a neighborhood, that's a zoo with nobody working the front desk.

cards.question: Isaiah keeps going with the animals settling into Edom's ruins. What does he say the owl will do there?

answers.text: Fly off to find a new home

cards.text: Even the birds of prey will gather there, each with its mate. Then Isaiah says, "Search and read the scroll of the LORD:" and see what it says about these creatures.

cards.question: True or false: Isaiah says that if you search the scroll of the LORD, you'll find some of these creatures missing.
Isaiah says not one of the creatures in Edom will lack her mate. Why?

answers.text: The LORD ordered it by His mouth
The land has plenty of water
The people of Edom feed them

cards.text: He will gather them by His Spirit, and His hand has measured out their portion. No princes left in Edom, but every single owl gets an assigned seat.

cards.question: The LORD has given the creatures their portion of Edom. True or false: Isaiah says they will hold it for only a single season.

findings.problem: The card asks the baker to guess the wording of Isaiah's simile: what the stars will fall 'like' (withered leaves vs torches vs the sun). Nothing earlier lets the baker reason to 'withered leaves'. It is like the Psalm 23 'anoint with oil' example. Card 6 leans the same way, since it tests the 'rolled up like a scroll' wording rather than meaning.

rule.text: Ask about the movement and the meaning: what changes, what the picture is, why the speaker says what he says. Never ask the baker to guess the next words of a line.

findings.problem: This story card tells nothing new from the passage. It repeats 'Rolled up like a scroll!' from the card 6/7 answers and adds only a joke. That makes it a recap card. The joke should ride on a card that moves the passage forward, for example one that carries 'All the stars of heaven will be dissolved' from 34:4, which the walkthrough never tells.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards. ... Every story card tells part of the passage. Jokes ride along on those cards.

findings.problem: The question's setup says 'No people will pass through Edom anymore' and then asks who will possess it. That rules out the wrong answer 'Shepherds and their flocks', leaving only two real options.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: 'All her princes will come to nothing, so there's nobody left to look after Edom's towers and fortresses' adds a cause-and-effect link that the text doesn't state. Isaiah 34:12-13 never says the towers are overgrown because the princes are gone.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: The question repeats the unstated link from card 8 ('Nobody's left to look after Edom's towers and fortresses') as the reason for the thorns and thistles. It also uses that link as the setup for the answer.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: 'with desert creatures, hyenas and wild goats calling to one another' reads as all three calling to one another. In Isaiah 34:14 the desert creatures meet with hyenas, and only the wild goats call to one another.

rule.text: Retelling: Papa Dorin can retell in his own words and fill in what the text clearly implies. Scene-setting details are fine. He never says anything the text shows is wrong.

findings.problem: The right answer 'The LORD ordered it by His mouth' keeps the biblical phrasing 'by His mouth'. The wrong answers ('The land has plenty of water', 'The people of Edom feed them') are plain modern wording, so the right answer stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike. None should sound more like the Bible, or more modern, than the others.
